_doc: Who says what, when. For each person, the first topic whose `when` holds and that has not been said (if `once`) plays; otherwise `idle`. Conditions: quest_step [quest, step], quest_active, quest_done, flag, not_flag. Effects (`do`): start_quest, flag, service (opens a service after the talk: stash, travel, respec, bestiary). Talking always tells the campaign 'talk <person>'. Lines: one or two short sentences.

ysolde.name: Captain Ysolde Marr

lines: So you're the Ninth. You're shorter than the stories.
The Order drilled in the yard behind the west houses. Targets are still standing. Nobody's used them in years.
Go and remember which end of that staff the light comes out of. Then come back and stand the wall with me.
Stay by me. They're coming through the gate. Keep your light up and don't let them circle you.
She's gone again. Nim. Climbed down the east wall at dawn and walked off toward Hollin's Ford.
Said she could hear a school bell. There's no school left out there. There's no Hollin's Ford left out there.
The east road's open. Bring her back. Then I'm nailing her boots to the floor.
You brought her back. I owe you a drink and an apology.
Mostly the drink. The gate opens for you now. Don't make me regret it.
Seven heartbeats of dark and the Glasswood came knocking. They took Nim Saltry off the wall-walk.
I'd send soldiers. Soldiers don't come back from the Dusk. Lamplighters sometimes did.
Light the old waylamps as you go. Each one is a place the dark has to remember to fear.
And if you meet something that talks... don't let it finish its sentences.

idle: Gate's behind me. Tallow's behind the gate. The rest is yours.

hask.name: Hask

lines: Easy with the light, Lamplighter. I'm only half of what you'd be hitting.
The girl? The Glazier took her to the stone ring. It collects things that shine.
Ask yourself why the Dusk wanted a child who maps the wall. Then don't ask me.
Your predecessor asked better questions. Look where it got him. Cairn by the deer trail.

idle: Still here. Still half. Go on.

nim.name: Nim Saltry

lines: Shh. Lesson's starting. It always starts now.
I can't leave. When the clocks strike four I'm back at my desk. The Mayor keeps the time.
Break his watch, Lamplighter. He's in the square under the big clock. He thinks you're late.
I was in that classroom so long I learned the same lesson four hundred times. It was about the sun.
The teacher said: 'At four o'clock the sun went to sleep, and we were so glad.' Everyone clapped. Every time.
I drew everything I saw out there. Want to go somewhere? I'll show you the way.
You took your time. I counted. Four thousand one hundred heartbeats.
It kept asking where the Lantern's heart is. I lied. I'm very good at lying.
Lamplighter... it wasn't angry. It was scared. Of you. Of that lantern.
Walk me home? The gate's back the way you came.

idle: Home's that way. I know a shortcut. It's mostly screaming.

ottilie.name: Mother Ottilie Brask

lines: There you are. Ninth of the Order, and the first in forty years. Let me look at you.
This is your staff. Hook at the top, lantern on the hook. Every Lamplighter before you carried one like it.
The lantern is not a lamp. It is a little of the Great Lantern's own fire. What you cast, you cast out of it.
Its Light is the circle around you. Inside it, the Dusk is only what it is. Outside, it is more. Stay in your light.
Getting hit dims it. Putting things down feeds it. You'll learn the rest the way we all did.
Captain Marr is at the gate. She'll want to see you hold that staff the right way up.
Nim's home. Good. Sit. No — stand, you'll fall asleep.
It asked her where the Lantern's heart is? Then it knows the Lantern has one.
The road lamps on the Ember Road went out the same night. Something is eating light out there.
Relight the road. Follow the moths. And don't look into anything that glows back.
The Matron's dead? Then why are your hands shaking? ...Mine too.
Teague used to come back like that. Before he stopped coming back.
Rest. Tomorrow I'll tell you what the Lantern burns. Maybe.
Teague's note says to ask you what the Great Lantern burns.
Oil. Wick. Stubbornness. Ask me again when you've earned the answer.
You're back without her. Then go out again. The Lantern can wait. Nim can't.
Need your points straightened out? I keep the order's ledger.

idle: Mind the Lantern. It's older than both of us and twice as grumpy.

fenn.name: Auntie Fenn Caddock

lines: WHAT? Speak up, I've been hitting things since dawn.
Bring me embers from the Dusk. Kindle, Temper, Quench, Anneal. I'll make your gear sing.
Mind the Heat. Every blow takes some out of the metal. When it's cold, it's done.

idle: ANVIL'S HOT. PUT SOMETHING ON IT.

lio.name: Lio Quill

lines: A bell. Cast by the order. Year one. 'To be rung only at noon.'
Noon. There hasn't been a noon in three hundred years. Unless... the bell is why.
Lamplighter, I think we didn't lose the sun. I think we put it to bed.
Three notes in the same hand. 'It is remembering.' Remembering what? It's darkness.
Unless it isn't. Unless it's a dream, and dreams are made of memories.
Take this. Teague's old watch-coat. It was in a box marked NINTH.
Careful — that jar is a Tuesday. Don't open it.
I study what the Dusk rewrites. Kill something new out there and I'll write it down.
And Teague left notes behind him, everywhere he went. Bring me every one.

idle: The bestiary's on the shelf. Mind the jar.

mara.name: Mara Brennick

lines: ...Then he's still fishing. He'd like that.
Take the lantern Ottilie gave him. He won't need it now.
My da went fishing in the Glasswood the night the glass came. He hasn't come home.
If you see him... tell him the tea's getting cold.

idle: Tuesdays I still make two cups.

odile.name: Odile Vane

lines: Lamps lit. The river's quieter. Not quiet. Quieter.
Up the falls, across the marsh, there's a belfry nobody built. Every night at the same hour, it rings.
The north path's open now the lamps hold. Don't follow lights in the marsh. Follow the road.
A Lamplighter. On my river. Ottilie's finally desperate.
The water started climbing the night your Great Lantern blinked. Coincidence, I'm sure.
My lamps went out with it. Light them and I'll ferry you anywhere the river still goes.

idle: Mind the edges. The river remembers falling down, sometimes. Mostly it doesn't.

wren.name: Wren Aldous
idle: First loaf of the day. Every day now. You did that.

lines: Fresh loaf? It's the— no. It's the first. It didn't burn.
There's a brick in my oven door and I don't remember putting it there. But I remember your face.
Nothing in this town stays warm past four. These did. Take them.
Fresh loaf? It's the fourth one t— you've got a look on you.
The door. Eight minutes to four, it sticks. ...How would you know about my door?
Fine. I'll wedge it with a brick. If I'm mad, at least the bread won't burn.
Fresh loaf? It's the fourth one today. It's always the fourth.
The first three burned. The oven door sticks at eight minutes to four and I never catch it in time.
Odd. I feel like I've told you that before.
Never mind. Fourth loaf. Always the fourth.
Fresh loaf? Fourth one today. It's always the fourth.

ansel.name: Master Ansel Crake
idle: Sit, sit. The lesson is the same as yesterday. That is rather the point of it.

lines: It's Wednesday. I have no Wednesday lesson. I have never needed one.
I shall have to teach them something new. I'd forgotten how frightening that is.
Nearly four. I ring the bell at four, and then it is a quarter past three again.
I used to think I'd dreamt it. Now I keep the chalk in my left pocket, because yesterday I kept it in my right.
A visitor! Sit anywhere but the third desk. Nim Saltry sits there. Every day, apparently.
Today's lesson is written on the board: 'Tuesday. The sun is resting. Be quiet.'
Who wrote it? I did. I think. The chalk is mine. The handwriting is mine. I don't remember the morning.
Quarter past three, half past. The children are very good. They have had a great deal of practice.
...six hundred and twelve. SIX HUNDRED AND THIRTEEN!
Nobody's ever heard thirteen! I'm going to count to a thousand and nobody can stop me!
...six hundred and nine, six hundred and ten — shh! I'm nearly there.
I always get to twelve and then the bell goes and I'm back at one.
Two hundred and six, two hundred and seven...
Master Crake says if I reach a thousand I can go home. I don't think he knows I can't.
